entries.a9525b92106c9fde: With “kyosei (tomoiki)” as its corporate philosophy, the company operates as a community-based real estate business centered on Kobe, Akashi and the Hanshin area. In its core condominium sales, the company says it will basically pursue convenient, well-located sites that leverage the advantages of local presence, while working to expand its business area into surrounding regions, and will advance strengthening quality, improving service, and offering a variety of plans in line with diversifying customer lifestyles. As a diversification of its exit strategy, the company is also working on developing and selling small income properties and housing facilities for the elderly, and in its detached house business it will focus on land acquisition to aim for stable annual supply volume. In the rental business, the company aims to improve its rental assets as a whole by maintaining occupancy and flexibly replacing properties, and as new businesses it will also work on developing grid-connected battery storage stations and non-asset businesses such as renovation and resale brokerage targeting buyers of the company's properties. The theme of the medium-term management plan (the fiscal year ended February 2027 to the fiscal year ended February 2029) is set as “Strengthening the Management Foundation”.

entries.ed4c320f36c9e9a7: For condominiums, the company aims for buildings that are safe and secure as a basis and harmonize with the streetscape; it was quick to take up the development of designer condominiums and specializes in advanced housing that incorporates functionality, convenience and comfort. Under the motto “Building condominiums that protect customers' lives and property”, it places emphasis on quality and conducts development with a focus on asset value and safety. Because it has no in-house sales department and outsources all sales externally, it adopts a strategy of appealing to customers through product strength in planning and design, with “building condominiums that sell” as its keyword.
